summary: The LAUNCH ANCHOR (cinatra#2809, per-scope surfaces S3, epic #2806) — the operator-upgrade twin of two fresh-install bootstrap halves widened in the SAME PR: the agent_runs column entry (src/lib/drizzle-store.ts) and assistantThreadSchemaQueries (src/lib/assistant-thread-schema.ts), both spreading the statements built by src/lib/launch-scope-anchor.ts. WHY: a run and a thread are now launched FROM a vantage — the workspace, an organization, a team, a project, or a person's own scope — and the vantage a launch was made from is the instance's canonical HOME, so a scoped instance has one address and a bookmark keeps resolving to it. The payload is the closed LaunchScopeAnchorV1 union ({v:1,kind:'workspace'} or {v:1,kind:'organization'|'team'|'project'|'user',id}), read by src/lib/launch-scope-anchor.ts and by nothing else. A COLUMN OF ITS OWN because every column that could have answered the question moves — assistant_threads.project_id is the resource-project-move key, an org membership changes, a run's actor can be re-pointed — and an address derived from a moving column moves with it. Written once from the exact launch route and never updated; composed and recurring descendants inherit the parent's anchor; headless, A2A and global writers persist none. TWO CHANGES: agent_runs and assistant_threads each gain the nullable launch_scope_anchor jsonb column. ADDITIVE, NULLABLE AND WITHOUT BACKFILL: a row that predates the column reads NULL, resolves to UNANCHORED and stays on the flat bare route labelled Legacy — inventing a home for a launch nobody recorded would be recording a launch nobody made, which is also why nothing is set NOT NULL and no other column is consulted to repair a malformed payload. Idempotent: both statements are ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, so this is a no-op on a database the bootstrap already created wide and a widening on every deployed one, and it writes to no existing row. NOT destructive: two nullable columns added, no key changed, no index replaced, nothing deleted. DOWN drops both columns, returning every instance to the flat bare route it was on before this migration. SEQ 0101 — strictly greater than the max shipped seq on the default branch (core__0100). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: maintainer approval required; the lane never merges.
